image_prompt.text: A grid-based labyrinth of about 31 by 31 cells, walls built from plain rectangular blocks in dark gray, roughly 10 studs tall and 2 studs thick, with open walkable paths about 6 studs wide between them
A single continuous light gray floor plane running underneath the entire maze
A clearly marked start tile in green set into the maze floor on one outer edge
A clearly marked end tile in red set into the maze floor on the opposite outer edge

layout_placement.text: The player's entry point at the green start tile on one edge of the maze
The maze's goal at the red end tile on the opposite edge, reachable from the start along a solvable path

notes: Preset caveat: took the Maze / Labyrinth preset on its own shape but dropped both of its options. `path-loop` is contradicted by the stated recursive-backtracker algorithm, which produces a perfect maze with dead ends and no cycles; `collectible-nodes` was dropped because the goal is start-to-end traversal and the prompt asks for no carryable items.
P6 retained from `puzzle-maze`: the maze must be solvable start to end by construction, which is exactly what the prompt asks for, so it is generated procedurally and dressed afterward.

The exposed attributes (MazeSize 31x31, WallHeight 10, PathWidth 6, WallThickness 2, WallColor dark gray, FloorColor light gray, Seed 12345) are scripting parameters rather than layout picks. The spatial ones are carried in `text`; `count` is omitted because these are dimensions and a grid extent, not a quantity of one pick. Seed and attribute exposure are Mechanics, out of layout scope.
